identity.name: County Palatine of Cephalonia and Zakynthos (Tocco)
identity.wikipedia: County Palatine of Cephalonia and Zakynthos

land.text: Cephalonia, Zakynthos and possibly Ithaca: 'In 1357, Robert of Taranto ceded Cephalonia, Zakynthos and Ithaca to the governor of Corfu, Leonardo I Tocco'

predecessors.note: After John II Orsini died the islands 'were occupied by the Angevins' (1335/36), and Robert of Taranto held them 1336-1357 (County Palatine page). Robert was an Angevin prince of Taranto, so kingdom-of-naples is my reading of 'the Angevins'; Cliopatria has no Angevin shape on the islands (its Byzantine Empire shape of 1352-1362 overlaps three grid cells of them, an artefact for the Byzantine dossier). The county itself dates from 1185 (Margaritus of Brindisi, then the Orsini): see notes.

land.text: the Tocco islands (Cephalonia, Zakynthos, Ithaca, Lefkada) with Angelokastron, joined to Ioannina under Carlo I Tocco: 'The Tocco ... were successful in gaining control over the Despotate of Epirus in 1411', and Glarentza (taken from Achaea in 1408)

successors.note: Carlo I Tocco 'was invited as the successor of his uncle Esau de' Buondelmonti in Ioannina' in February 1411 and 'ruled as the Despot of Epirus from 1411' (Carlo I Tocco page); he was granted the title despotes in 1415. The Epirus dossier records the same union as a merge in February 1411; Cliopatria draws the islands inside Epirus only from 1415 and ends its House of Tocco row in 1414. Glarentza (seized from Achaea in 1408) passes with the islands in February 1411 and is lost to Centurione II Zaccaria in July 1414, an event of the Epirus dossier.

capitals.name: Castle of Saint George (Kastro Agiou Georgiou), near Peratata, Cephalonia
capitals.note: Infobox capital of the county ('Castle of Saint George (near Peratata)'); the page does not date the seat under the Tocco. The coordinates are my estimate (the gazetteer has no entry).

rulers.name: Leonardo I Tocco
rulers.title: Count palatine of Cephalonia and Zakynthos
rulers.note: County Palatine page: 'Leonardo I ruled 1357-1376'; the Leonardo I Tocco page says he 'died sometime between March 1375 and August 1377'.

rulers.name: Carlo I Tocco
rulers.title: Count palatine of Cephalonia and Zakynthos, duke of Leukas
rulers.note: 'succeeded his father as count of Cephalonia and duke of Leukas on the latter's death in 1376'. From February 1411 he ruled Ioannina too and was despot of Epirus until 4 July 1429 (Epirus dossier). His brother Leonardo II was 'invested with the island of Zante as appanage in 1399'.

correction.text: the 1363 shape unchanged, applied from 1357: Cephalonia, Zakynthos and possibly Ithaca, named by Robert of Taranto

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe for 1357-1361, which Cliopatria lacks (its row starts in 1363). 'Robert named him Count palatine of Cephalonia, Zakynthos and possibly Ithaca as well'; the County Palatine page: 'In 1357, Robert of Taranto ceded Cephalonia, Zakynthos and Ithaca'. Neither page gives an area, so the shape's 1,819 km2 (three grid cells here) cannot be compared with an infobox figure.

correction.text: the 1375 shape (the three islands plus Lefkada), applied from 1362 to 1374: 'Probably by ca. 1362, and certainly before 1373, Leonardo also succeeded in gaining control over Lefkada and the port of Vonitsa'

keyframe_review.note: 1,819 km2 for 1363-1374 lacks Lefkada, which Cliopatria adds only in 1375 (bbox to 38.87 N); the page has Leonardo in control of it by ca. 1362 and certainly before 1373. Vonitsa is a mainland port outside both Cliopatria shapes and is not drawn (one grid cell would be larger than the town's reach).

2,210 km2 for 1375-1406: Cephalonia, Zakynthos, Ithaca and Lefkada under Leonardo I (died between March 1375 and August 1377) and Carlo I, who succeeded 'on the latter's death in 1376'; the infobox gives no area. Not drawn, because the pages give no end for them: Corinth and Megara, which Carlo 'seized in 1395' by his Acciaioli marriage, (page silent on its end). Glarentza, 'seized in 1407-1408 by his brother Leonardo' (Carlo I Tocco page), is drawn from 1408 (house-of-tocco_1408). Zante became Leonardo II's appanage in 1399 without leaving the family.

correction.text: the 1407 shape plus Angelokastron and its surroundings (an 18 km circle at 21.2 E 38.55 N, approximate), for 1407 only; from 1408 use house-of-tocco_1408, which adds Glarentza

keyframe_review.note: 2,210 km2 for 1407-1414, the same land as before; no page explains Cliopatria's 1407 split. Muriq Shpata page: in 1406 Pal Shpata 'ceded Angelokastron to the Ottomans' and Carlo Tocco 'captured it within less than a year' (the Carlo page has it 'from 1405', marked dubious). The state ends in February 1411, three years before Cliopatria's row, and the same land is Epirus land from then (see successors). Glarentza joins in 1408 (house-of-tocco_1408).

correction.text: the 1407 shape plus Angelokastron (an 18 km circle at 21.2 E 38.55 N) plus Glarentza (Glarentza (Clarenza, Kyllini), the Achaean port and mint, a 15 km circle at 21.13 E 37.94 N, the same circle as principality-of-achaea's ledger), for 1408 to February 1411: 'Leonardo and Carlo conquered Glarentza in 1408'

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe for 1408-1411. Glarentza is held from 1408 (Centurione II Zaccaria page; Carlo I Tocco page: 'in 1407-1408 his brother Leonardo seized and plundered the fortress'; Glarentza page: 'In late 1407') and the state ends in February 1411, when the land passes to the Despotate of Epirus; the loss of Glarentza in July 1414 is then Epirus's. The circle takes one grid cell (about 253 km2), a guess at the port's reach. [Reviewer eu-05-f finding, repaired 2026-10-19.]

ledger.note: 1357: Robert of Taranto makes Leonardo I Tocco count palatine of Cephalonia, Zakynthos and Ithaca. Page: 'Robert named him Count palatine of Cephalonia, Zakynthos and possibly Ithaca as well'; County Palatine page: 'In 1357, Robert of Taranto ceded Cephalonia, Zakynthos and Ithaca to the governor of Corfu, Leonardo I Tocco.' Ithaca is 'possibly' on one page and certain on the other.

region.text: Lefkada (Leucas), the island that Cliopatria adds in 1375, drawn as the 1375 shape minus the 1363 shape

ledger.counterpart: previous holders of Lefkada and Vonitsa (page silent)
ledger.note: ca. 1362: Leonardo I gains Lefkada and the port of Vonitsa. Page: 'Probably by ca. 1362, and certainly before 1373, Leonardo also succeeded in gaining control over Lefkada and the port of Vonitsa'; the page names no grantor or previous holder. Vonitsa is not drawn.

region.text: Angelokastron and its surroundings on the Aetolian mainland (an 18 km circle at 21.2 E 38.55 N, approximate)

ledger.note: 1407: Carlo I Tocco takes Angelokastron. Muriq Shpata page: in 1406 Pal Shpata 'ceded Angelokastron to the Ottomans' and Carlo Tocco 'captured it within less than a year'; the Carlo I Tocco page has him holding it 'from 1405' (marked dubious). The year is the later reading. [Reviewer eu-05-f, 2026-10-19: counterpart despotate-of-arta to ottoman-empire: the Muriq Shpata page has 'Paul ceded Angelokastron to the Ottomans (only for Carlo Tocco to capture it within less than a year)', so Carlo took it from the Ottomans (despotate-of-arta records the 1406 cession).]

region.text: Glarentza, the port and mint of the Principality of Achaea (a 15 km circle at 21.13 E 37.94 N, approximate), seized by Leonardo II Tocco for the family

ledger.note: 1408: Leonardo and Carlo Tocco take Glarentza from the Principality of Achaea. Centurione II Zaccaria page: 'Leonardo and Carlo conquered Glarentza in 1408 the greatest sea port of the Principality'; Carlo I Tocco page: 'in 1407-1408 his brother Leonardo seized and plundered the fortress of Glarentza, in the northwestern Morea'; the Glarentza page has it 'in late 1407' ('Centurione's own brother-in-law Leonardo II Tocco seized Glarentza and reaped an enormous booty'), so the year is the Centurione page's 1408 with 1407 as the page-allowed alternative. The mirror of principality-of-achaea ledger 1408 (loss to house-of-tocco). The Toccos did not keep it: Centurione retook it in July 1414 ('a Venetian-mediated deal restored the city to Centurione in July 1414', Glarentza page; 'was able to retake Glarentza and expel the Toccos', Centurione page). By then the county was inside Carlo's despotate of Epirus (February 1411), so the 1414 loss is despotate-of-epirus's event, not this dossier's. [Reviewer eu-05-f finding, repaired 2026-10-19.]

region.text: the Tocco islands with Angelokastron, joined to Ioannina in one rule, and Glarentza (taken from Achaea in 1408)

ledger.note: February 1411: Carlo I Tocco is invited to Ioannina and unites it with the islands. Page: he 'was invited as the successor of his uncle Esau de' Buondelmonti in Ioannina' in February 1411 and 'ruled as the Despot of Epirus from 1411'; County Palatine page: 'successful in gaining control over the Despotate of Epirus in 1411'. Despot title from Manuel II in 1415.

region.text: the Tocco islands with Angelokastron, and Glarentza (taken from Achaea in 1408)

ledger.note: 1411: the Tocco county is absorbed into Carlo I's Despotate of Epirus. The county itself lasts to 1479 inside that despotate (Epirus dossier); this dossier ends in 1411 so that the land is not claimed twice, three years before Cliopatria's row ends (1414).

wars.name: Tocco-Spata wars

zones.text: Angelokastron and its surroundings on the Aetolian mainland (an 18 km circle at 21.2 E 38.55 N, approximate)

wars.outcome: Carlo I's siege of Angelokastron (1402-03) was repulsed and his 1406 raid on Acarnania and Arta failed to take the city, but Angelokastron fell to him within a year of Pal Shpata's 1406 cession to the Ottomans; the Albanians beat the Tocco army at Kranea in 1412 and Carlo took Arta only in October 1416, as despot of Epirus.
wars.note: Same war as the entry in despotate-of-arta. The Tocco county ends in February 1411; the later years are Epirus's. The Carlo I Tocco page adds a 1412 victory for the Albanians who 'failed to take Ioannina' and the 1412 marriage of Carlo's daughter to the Ottoman prince Musa Celebi.

certainty.note: The island coasts are fixed by the sea, but who held Lefkada, Vonitsa and the mainland fortresses at which date rests on pages that say 'ca. 1362', 'from 1405' or 'within less than a year'.

notes:
SCOPE. Wikipedia's county palatine of Cephalonia and Zakynthos lasts 1185-1479 (Margaritus of Brindisi 1185, Matthew Orsini 1195, Orsini and Angevin rule to 1357, the Tocco 1357-1479; County Palatine page). Cliopatria's 'House of Tocco' row is only 1363-1414 and shares Wikidata Q149846 with that article. This dossier covers the Tocco county from the 1357 grant (page) to February 1411, when Carlo I Tocco also became ruler of Ioannina: from then the islands are carried by the despotate-of-epirus dossier (its ledger has a matching merge of house-of-tocco in February 1411, its keyframes draw the islands from 1415 and Vonitsa with the islands to 1479). Rule 2 (one colour for a state's life) would put 1185-1357 in this dossier too; the pages give the rulers and suzerains but Cliopatria has no shapes and other Cliopatria rows may draw the islands then, and the page budget (two pages) was spent, so a gap-filler should extend the dossier back to 1185 or write the Orsini-era county as the same state.

CLIOPATRIA. 1363-1374 lacks Lefkada (ledger 1362); the 1407 split has no explanation; the row's end in 1414 is three years late against the 1411 merge; Byzantine Empire 1352-1362 overlaps three grid cells of the islands.

NOT DRAWN, PAGE SILENT ON THE END. Corinth and Megara 'seized in 1395' (Carlo I Tocco page; claimed through Francesca Acciaioli); Vonitsa, which the Hospitallers took in April 1378 (Gjin Bua Shpata page) though Leonardo had it by 1373; Zante as Leonardo II's appanage from 1399. No suzerain is named for 1357-1411 (the Leonardo page has him in a 1374 delegation offering Achaea to Joan I of Naples), so no vassal event is written. Counterpart 'kingdom-of-naples' for 1357 is my reading of Robert of Taranto.

FAMILY. 'balkans' because colours.json already assigns house-of-tocco hue 75 (that family); the Epirus dossier uses 'rome'. Gazetteer names needed: Cephalonia, Zakynthos, Ithaca, Lefkada, Vonitsa, Angelokastron, Peratata (Castle of Saint George).

REPAIR 2026-10-19 (reviewer eu-05-f, finding 2). Glarentza added: 1408 gain from principality-of-achaea (mirror of the Achaea ledger's 1408 loss; Centurione II Zaccaria page '... conquered Glarentza in 1408', Carlo I Tocco page '1407-1408', Glarentza page 'late 1407': the pages differ by a year, 1408 kept to match the Achaea ledger); new keyframe house-of-tocco_1408 (1408-1411); Glarentza added to the successor land and to the merge and dissolve regions so it passes to despotate-of-epirus in February 1411. The end is known: Centurione retook it in July 1414 (Glarentza page; 'At 1414' on the Centurione page), which is a 1414 loss for despotate-of-epirus (that dossier's ledger has the 1421 purchase from Oliverio Franco and the 1428 handover but no 1414 loss) and should replace house-of-tocco as counterpart of principality-of-achaea's 1414 gain. Circle used: 21.13 E 37.94 N, 15 km, one grid cell, identical to the Achaea ledger's. Not repaired (thin, for a gap-filler): county palatine 1185-1357, who held Lefkada before ca. 1362, Corinth and Megara 1395, Vonitsa 1362-1378, and the reading of kingdom-of-naples as the 1357 counterpart (principality-of-achaea fits the County Palatine page better).
